To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the numerical model of transformation plasticity is in good quantitative and qualitative agreement with analytical solutions for transformation plasticity and experimental data for transformation plasticity.

a two-dimensional numerical model of transformation plasticity for an elastic–plastic material is able to capture the main trends observed experimentally and predicted analytically for the α/γ transformation in iron, and that the numerical model can be used for a wide range of materials with different transformation mismatch and yield stresses.

the numerical model presented in this paper is able to reproduce the linear relationship between the applied stress and the accumulated plastic strain for low stresses and the non-linear relationship for high stresses.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of numerical models for the analysis of the mechanical behavior of materials that undergo phase transformations under the application of mechanical loads.
the development of numerical models to simulate superplastic flow in metals.
the development and implementation of a numerical model for transformation superplasticsity in an elastic, ideally-plastic material, and its validation with experimental data for iron.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the numerical model presented here is in excellent agreement with existing analytical models and experimental results for transformation superplasting of an ideally plastic material, and can therefore be considered as a reliable numerical model for transformation superplasitcity in a real material.
this numerical model is able to predict the transformation superplastic behaviour of pure iron.

the numerical model of transformation mismatch superplasticity is in good agreement with analytical predictions for a wide range of conditions and that this model provides an excellent basis for the development of more sophisticated constitutive equations for transformation superplastics.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

a two-dimensional plane strain model can be used to simulate the transformation superplastic behaviour of an ideally plastic material with a temperature dependent yield stress and transformation mismatch.
transformation superplastic behavior can be described in an ideally plastic model using a plane-strain equivalent of the transformation mismatch.

the present numerical model is capable of predicting the strain hardening behavior of transformation superplasticy in pure iron, and the numerical model can serve as an effective tool in predicting the strain hardenability of transformation superplasty in other materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
transformation superplastic deformation can be accurately modelled using a two-dimensional numerical model for a plane-strain deformation state.
a two-dimensional numerical model can provide a good approximation of the transformation mismatch in a three-dimensional material.
the analytical solutions for transformation plasticity are applicable to a wider range of conditions than previously thought.
